_about: Numbers the Python and JavaScript halves of the engine share. Typed here once; both read this file (vslib.CONTRACTS, lib/paths.mjs CONTRACTS). A studio's profile.json → checks may tighten the reading numbers for its own videos.

sizes._about: The two shapes the kit lays out: [width, height] in pixels.

fps._about: What a new video renders at, and the rates the kit has been proven at (others may work; vs check warns).

phone_safe._about: A vertical video in a phone's full-screen player (LinkedIn measured, Sep 2026), as fractions of the frame: the status bar covers the top, the caption and scrubber the bottom, each side is cropped, and the button rail covers the right edge between rail.y and the caption.

reading._about: How long words need on screen. title_min_secs: the shortest title that read (the Lab reel v13, after cold viewers called v12's 0.94 s titles 'words flying across the screen'); words_per_sec: subtitle convention, about 180 words a minute.

checks._about: The thresholds of the checks a reviewer can tune (profile.json → checks overrides any of them). Reading time uses reading above. vs inspect: two_zones_words (a scene showing at least this many words while a title is up is a second reading zone; one or two words are a picture's labels), offscreen_rest_secs (an element parked partly off the frame this long), dead_air_secs (nothing but the backdrop on screen this long). qa.py: cues_per_10s (sound effects in any ten seconds; the busiest approved explainer peaks at 13), loudness_lufs ± loudness_tolerance and true_peak_dbtp (the final mix), flash_jump (the whole frame's mean brightness, 0–255, changing this much from one frame to the next).

stages._about: A video's stages in order, for Review Studio's top line (where you are in the whole process). vs review open --stage names a round's; vs review step --stage marks one reached outside a round.

plain._about: Every check in plain words, for the human in Review Studio: name = what it found (a heading), says = what that means for the video. The finding's own text gives the specifics; vs review advise adds Claude's recommendation.

covers.name: A shape covers words
covers.says: Something is painted over words, so they can't be read while it's there.

line-through.name: A line runs through words
line-through.says: A drawn line crosses the words.

on-photo.name: Words on a picture with nothing behind them
on-photo.says: The words sit straight on a busy picture, which makes them hard to read.

low-contrast.name: Words hard to read on their background
low-contrast.says: The words and what's behind them are too close in brightness.

title-on-scene.name: A title lands on the drawing
title-on-scene.says: A title appears on top of the scene's own drawing.

straddles.name: Words half on a shape, half off
straddles.says: The words sit across the edge of a shape.

spills.name: Words run past their card's edge
spills.says: The words don't fit inside the card they belong to.

phone-safe.name: Words where a phone covers the picture
phone-safe.says: On a phone, the buttons and captions sit over this spot, so the words would be hidden.

on-text.name: Two sets of words overlap
on-text.says: Words are on top of other words.

two-zones.name: A title and the scene's words at the same time
two-zones.says: The viewer has two things to read at once.

fast-text.name: Words gone before they can be read
fast-text.says: The words leave the screen faster than a person reads them.

offscreen-at-rest.name: Something parked partly off the screen
offscreen-at-rest.says: It sits half off the edge, not moving, as if it were cut off.

keep-clear.name: Something entered a zone you said to keep clear

done-changed.name: A scene you called done has changed
done-changed.says: It no longer matches the version you approved.

done-gone.name: A scene you called done is gone

covered.name: Something bright near a phone's edges
covered.says: A phone covers the outer edges of a vertical video: the clock bar at the top and a sliver at each side.

blacks.name: A black that doesn't match the rest
blacks.says: This stretch's dark background is a different shade from the rest of the video.

black-hole.name: A pure-black frame near a cut
black-hole.says: Most of the frame goes fully black for a moment near a cut.

audio-drop.name: The sound drops out
audio-drop.says: The sound falls far below its usual level here.

flash.name: The whole frame flashes
flash.says: The picture jumps sharply brighter or darker in a single frame.

loudness.name: The mix is too loud or too quiet
loudness.says: The overall level is off from what platforms expect.

true-peak.name: The mix peaks too high
true-peak.says: The loudest moments may distort on some speakers.

cue-density.name: Too many sound effects close together
cue-density.says: Many effects land within ten seconds, which can feel busy.

dead-air.name: Nothing on screen but the background
dead-air.says: For a moment the picture is empty: a scene waiting for its word, or a handoff left bare.
